name: Gallinazo
description: Gallinazo is a distinct domino game played in Puerto Rico and parts of Mexico, characterized by its individual play format and unique penalty scoring system. While most domino games focus on partnership play, Gallinazo forces each of the four participants to hunt for themselves. The game is named after the 'vulture' (gallinazo), perhaps referring to the way players must 'prey' on others' mistakes to avoid being the one left holding highndvalue tiles. It is culturally synonymous with social stakes, where the cumulative loser is famously tasked with buying the next round of drinks for the table.

history.origins: Gallinazo is particularly associated with San Lorenzo, Puerto Rico, and Guadalajara, Mexico. It represents an informal, highndvelocity version of dominoes that prioritizes social interaction and 'secret' scoring to keep the tension high until the final round.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Regional popularity grows in Caribbean and Mexican social clubs.
1990s: Documented by researchers Jose Carrillo and Alfonso Garcia.
Present: Remains a popular 'tavern game' for determining social obligations.
history.cultural: The tradition of keeping scores secret until the 7th deal is a specific cultural trait of Gallinazo, designed to prevent players from 'teaming up' against the leader prematurely.
history.evolution: The game simplifies the branching paths of many domino variants into a single line of play, focusing the strategic depth on pip management rather than board control.

setup.players: Exactly 4 players, each playing for themselves.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 7 tiles, leaving no boneyard.

rules.objective: Avoid accumulating points. The player with the lowest total score after 7 deals wins; the player with the highest score is the loser.
rules.gameplay:
1. Matching: Play proceeds counter-clockwise. Tiles are played in a single line, matching the pips on the exposed ends.
2. Going Out: A deal ends when a player plays their last tile.
3. Scoring: When a player goes out, all other players sum the pips on their remaining tiles and add them to their cumulative score.
keyRules: Secret Scoring: The official scorer should keep the cumulative totals hidden until the final deal to maintain suspense.
Social Stake: The loser is traditionally responsible for providing 'social refreshments' (beer) for the group.

strategy.basic: Dump your 'heavies' early. High doublendtiles (6-6, 5-5) are a massive liability in Gallinazo. If you can't play them early, they will balloon your score if the deal ends suddenly.
strategy.intermediate: Pip Management: Toward the end of a deal, try to keep tiles that give you the most matching options (like a 1nd1 or 2nd2) rather than tiles with high pips. A low-value 'dead end' tile can be used to block the game if you are sure you have the lowest score.
strategy.advanced: The Block Trap: If you have a very low pip count (e.g., only a 0-1 and 1nd1 left), you may want to deliberately block the line. In Gallinazo, if you can block the game while holding the lowest count, you force every opponent to take a full point hit.
tips: If you are the last player to move, be extremely careful. If you block the game and someone else has a tie or lower score, your 4x penalty can end your chances for the entire match.
Pay attention to which suits (pip values) have been played 7 times. This tells you which ends are 'dead' and can be used to block.
In the 7th deal, play extremely conservatively. This is when the secret scores are revealed and the pressure is highest.
